title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.24073v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents now resolve repository issues and generate compact playable games, but whether they can build a large 3D game from scratch remains open. Such games tightly couple mechanics, scenes, assets, and interaction logic, and their quality rests on player enjoyment, which existing benchmarks rarely assess. Thus, we introduce 3D GameDev Arena, a first extreme long-horizon benchmark of 108 from-scratch game-development tasks across 14 genres. Given only a text specification and UI/UX reference images, a fully automated plan--implement--test--repair pipeline builds each task into a self-contained browser game. Runs average $\sim$1,000 LLM calls ; the longest uses 14,407 calls, 2.13B tokens, and 608 assets. Evaluation spans (1) objective code-level functional acceptance against the game specification, (2) agent-based QA and playtesting of 3D presentation and playability, and (3) blind pairwise Bradley-Terry human preference in a public

translated_title: 3D GameDev Arena：对能规划、构建并试玩测试超长时程浏览器游戏的编程智能体进行基准评测
translated_abstract: 编程智能体如今已能解决代码仓库问题并生成小型可玩游戏，但它们能否从零开始构建大型3D游戏仍是一个悬而未决的问题。这类游戏将游戏机制、场景、资产和交互逻辑紧密耦合在一起，其质量取决于玩家的游戏体验，而现有基准测试很少对此进行评估。因此，我们推出了3D GameDev Arena，这是首个覆盖14种游戏类型、共108项从零开始游戏开发任务的极限长时程基准。在仅给定文本规格说明和UI/UX参考图像的条件下，一个全自动的“规划—实现—测试—修复”流水线将每项任务构建为独立的浏览器游戏。每次运行平均需要约1,000次LLM调用；最长的一次运行使用了14,407次调用、21.3亿个token和608个资产。评估涵盖三个方面：(1) 对照游戏规格说明进行客观的代码级功能验收；(2) 基于智能体的3D呈现与可玩性质量保证及试玩测试；(3) 在公开环境中的盲测成对Bradley-Terry人类偏好评估（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 3D GameDev Arena是首个针对从零构建大型3D浏览器游戏的编程智能体极限长时程基准，通过108项跨14种游戏类型的任务，结合全自动“规划-实现-测试-修复”流水线，并从代码级功能验收、智能体试玩测试和人类偏好三个维度进行综合评估。
en_tdlr: 3D GameDev Arena introduces the first extreme long-horizon benchmark of 108 from-scratch 3D browser game development tasks across 14 genres, evaluating coding agents via a fully automated plan-implement-test-repair pipeline with code-level functional acceptance, agent-based playtesting, and blind human preference comparison.
